title: Pair Sprint
statement: Given an array of numbers and a target, return the indices of two values whose sum equals the target.

title: Bracket Dash
statement: Return true if every opened bracket is closed by the correct matching bracket.

title: Max Streak
statement: Return the maximum number of consecutive 1 values in a binary array.

title: Clean Duplicates
statement: Return the array with duplicates removed while keeping the first occurrence order.

title: First Unique
statement: Return the first character that appears exactly once. Return an empty string if none exists.

title: Merge Sorted
statement: Merge two sorted arrays into one sorted array.

title: Mirror Word
statement: Return true if the string is a palindrome after removing spaces and lowercasing letters.

title: Missing Level
statement: Given numbers from 0 to n with one missing value, return the missing value.

title: Most Frequent
statement: Return the value that appears most often. If several values tie, any tied value is valid.

title: Window Sum
statement: Return the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray with length k.

title: Island Count
statement: Count groups of connected 1 cells in a grid. Cells connect in four directions.

title: Daily Temperatures
statement: For each day, return how many days must pass until a warmer temperature appears.

title: Subarray Target
statement: Return true if there is a contiguous subarray whose sum equals target.

title: Longest Unique
statement: Return the length of the longest substring without repeated characters.

title: Grid Escape
statement: Return the shortest path length from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell. 1 means blocked, 0 means open.

title: Coin Race
statement: Given coin values and an amount, return the minimum number of coins needed to make that amount, or -1.

title: Course Unlock
statement: Return true if every course can be completed with the given prerequisite pairs.

title: Word Portal
statement: Return the minimum number of single-letter transformations from begin to end using only words from the list.

title: Signal Floor
statement: Given daily signal changes, return the lowest running signal level starting from zero.

title: Badge Cleaner
statement: Return the badge text with every non-letter character removed and all letters lowercased.

title: Checkpoint Gap
statement: Given sorted checkpoint positions, return the largest distance between neighboring checkpoints.

title: Majority Pulse
statement: Return the value that appears more than half of the time. If no such value exists, return null.

title: Range Compressor
statement: Given sorted unique numbers, compress consecutive runs into strings like '2->5' and single values like '8'.

title: Cooldown Profit
statement: Given prices, return the max profit when after selling you must wait one day before buying again.

title: Server Waves
statement: Given request times and a cooldown, return how many requests are accepted when each accepted request blocks the server until time + cooldown.

title: Diagonal Scan
statement: Return the sum of the main diagonal and anti-diagonal of a square matrix, counting the center only once.

title: Route Blacklist
statement: Given directed routes and blocked nodes, return true if destination can be reached from start without entering blocked nodes.

title: Memory Tiles
statement: Given a string of tiles and a dictionary, return true if the string can be fully split into dictionary words.

title: Cache Eviction
statement: Simulate an LRU cache. Given capacity and operations, return the output of every get operation, using -1 for misses.

title: Relay Optimizer
statement: Given sorted relay positions and k extra relays, minimize the maximum distance between neighboring relays and return that distance rounded down.

title: Even Signal
statement: Return how many numbers in the array are even.

title: Prefix Alarm
statement: Given numbers and a limit, return the first index where the running sum is greater than the limit, or -1 if it never happens.

title: Vowel Gate
statement: Return true if the string contains every vowel a, e, i, o and u at least once.

title: Nearest Zero
statement: Given a binary array containing at least one zero, return an array where each position stores its distance to the nearest zero.

title: Score Normalizer
statement: Return each score shifted so the minimum score becomes zero while preserving order.

title: Packet Window
statement: Given packet sizes and a limit, return the length of the longest contiguous window whose sum is at most the limit.

title: Ranked Votes
statement: Given an array of candidate names, return the top k names by vote count. Break ties alphabetically.

title: Level Bridges
statement: Given an undirected graph, return the fewest edges needed to travel from start to target, or -1 if unreachable.

title: Cooldown Scheduler
statement: Given task labels and cooldown n, return the minimum number of time slots needed to run all tasks so equal labels are separated by at least n slots.

title: Kth Signal
statement: Given an unsorted array and k, return the kth largest value.

title: Maze Checkpoints
statement: Given a grid with S, C, T, . and #, return the shortest path length from S to T that visits at least one C checkpoint. Return -1 if impossible.

title: Burst Combos
statement: Given positive combo values, return the maximum score from choosing non-adjacent combos.

title: Reverse Words Lite
statement: Given a sentence, return the words in reverse order. Extra spaces should be ignored and the answer should use single spaces.

title: Min Gap
statement: Given an array of numbers, return the minimum absolute difference between any two values. Return 0 when there are fewer than two values.

title: Digit Sum
statement: Given a non-negative integer, return the sum of its digits.

title: Anagram Groups Count
statement: Given words, return how many groups of anagrams exist. Words belong to the same group when their letters can be rearranged into each other.

title: Rotating Log
statement: Given event strings in the form login:name or logout:name, return the names still online after all events, sorted alphabetically.

title: Matrix Ring Sum
statement: Given a rectangular matrix, return the sum of the outer border cells. A cell on a one-row or one-column matrix should be counted once.

title: Weighted Checkpoints
statement: Given n nodes, weighted undirected edges [a,b,w], a start and a target, return the minimum travel cost. Return -1 if the target is unreachable.

title: Partition Balance
statement: Given positive numbers, split them into two groups so the absolute difference between group sums is as small as possible. Return that minimum difference.

title: Clamp Counter
statement: Given an array and inclusive bounds low and high, return how many numbers are inside the range.

title: Adjacent Pairs
statement: Return how many adjacent pairs contain the same value.

title: Running Peak
statement: Return an array where each position stores the maximum value seen from the start through that position.

title: Word Lengths
statement: Given words, return their lengths in the same order.

title: Missing Ticket
statement: Numbers contain every value from 1 to n except one missing value. Return the missing value.

title: Diagonal Pulse
statement: Given a square matrix, return the sum of both diagonals. If the center cell belongs to both diagonals, count it once.

title: Letter Balance
statement: Return the absolute difference between the number of vowels and consonants in a lowercase word.

title: Sign Flips
statement: Return how many times the sign changes between neighboring nonzero numbers. Zero values should be ignored.

title: Compress Runs
statement: Compress consecutive equal characters as character followed by count. Return an empty string for empty input.

title: Inventory Delta
statement: Given updates [item, delta], combine deltas per item and return [item, total] pairs sorted by item. Omit items whose total becomes 0.

title: Even Sum Span
statement: Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is even.

title: Server Load
statement: Given half-open intervals [start,end), return the maximum number of intervals active at the same time.

title: Island Perimeter Lite
statement: Given a grid of 0 water and 1 land cells, return the total perimeter of all land.

title: Top Words
statement: Return the k most frequent words. Sort by higher frequency first, then alphabetically for ties.

title: Limited Backpack
statement: Given item weights, item values and a capacity, return the maximum value using each item at most once.

title: Merge Windows
statement: Merge overlapping closed intervals and return the merged intervals sorted by start.

title: Min Jumps Forward
statement: Each number says how far you may jump forward from that index. Return the minimum jumps needed to reach the last index, or -1 if impossible.

title: Blocked Paths
statement: Given a grid where 1 means blocked and 0 means open, count paths from top-left to bottom-right moving only right or down.

title: Word Bridge
statement: Given start, target and words, return the minimum number of one-letter changes needed to reach target using only words from the list. Include the target word in the path count as a move result. Return -1 if impossible.

title: Course Cycle Check
statement: Given n courses and prerequisite pairs [before, after], return true if every course can be completed without a dependency cycle.

title: Edit Distance Lite
statement: Return the minimum number of insertions, deletions or replacements needed to transform string a into string b.

title: Parity Indexes
statement: Return the indices where the number parity matches the index parity.

title: Trim Zero Edges
statement: Remove zeros from the beginning and end of the array, but keep zeros in the middle.

title: Rotate Once
statement: Rotate the array one step to the right. Return an empty array if input is empty.

title: Title Initials
statement: Given a phrase, return the uppercase first letter of each non-empty word joined together.

title: Target Blocks
statement: Return how many contiguous blocks of the target value appear in the array.

title: Sorted Squares Lite
statement: Given a sorted array of integers, return the squares sorted in nondecreasing order.

title: Password Score Lite
statement: Return how many character groups appear in the password: lowercase, uppercase, digit and symbol.

title: Min Max Sum
statement: Return the sum of the minimum and maximum values in the array. Return 0 for an empty array.

title: Row Sums
statement: Return an array containing the sum of each matrix row.

title: First Longest Word
statement: Return the first word with the maximum length. Return an empty string when the list is empty.

title: Neighbor Gap Count
statement: Return how many neighboring pairs have an absolute difference less than or equal to limit.

title: Subarray Target Count
statement: Return how many contiguous subarrays have sum equal to target.

title: Window Average Threshold
statement: Given nums, window size k and threshold, return how many length-k windows have average at least threshold.

title: Decode Runs
statement: Decode a run-length string where each letter is followed by a positive single-digit count.

title: Column Peak
statement: Return the maximum value from each matrix column. The matrix is non-empty and rectangular.

title: Ticket Queue Time
statement: People buy one ticket per turn from left to right. Given ticket counts and an index k, return how many turns pass until person k finishes.

title: Nested Parentheses Score
statement: Score balanced parentheses: () is 1, AB is A+B, and (A) is 2*A.

title: Unique Paths Lite
statement: Given rows and cols, count paths from top-left to bottom-right moving only right or down.

title: Longest Balanced AB
statement: Given a string containing only a and b, return the length of the longest substring with the same number of a and b.

title: Dependency Order Lite
statement: Given n tasks and prerequisite pairs [before, after], return one valid order using the smallest available task first. Return [] if impossible.

title: Range Add Final
statement: Start with an array of n zeros. Each operation [l,r,x] adds x to every index from l to r inclusive. Return the final array.

title: Coin Change Min
statement: Given coin values and an amount, return the minimum number of coins needed. Return -1 if impossible.

title: LIS Length
statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

title: Network Delay Lite
statement: Given n nodes, directed edges [from,to,time] and a start node, return the time until all nodes receive the signal. Return -1 if some node is unreachable.

title: Palindrome Cuts
statement: Return the minimum number of cuts needed so every resulting substring is a palindrome.

title: Regex Dot Star Lite
statement: Return true if the full text matches a pattern containing lowercase letters, dot as any single character and star as zero or more of the previous token.

title: Max Square Area
statement: Given a binary matrix, return the area of the largest square containing only 1 values.

title: Min Cost Stairs Plus
statement: Each index has a cost. You may start at index 0 or 1 and climb 1 or 2 steps. Return the minimum cost to move past the last index.

title: Word Break Lite
statement: Return true if the string can be split into one or more words from the dictionary.

title: Signal Gap
statement: Given an array containing only 0 and 1, return the largest number of zeroes strictly between two consecutive 1 values. Return 0 if there are fewer than two 1 values.

title: Balance Marker
statement: Return the first index whose elements strictly to its left sum to the same value as elements strictly to its right. Return -1 if no such index exists. Values may be negative.

title: Circular Fuel
statement: At station i you receive gas[i] fuel and spend cost[i] to reach the next station on a circle. Starting with an empty tank, return the smallest starting index that completes one full lap, or -1 if impossible. Arrays have equal nonzero length and nonnegative values.

title: Painted Line
statement: Each pair [start, end] paints the half-open interval from start to end on a number line, with start <= end. Return the total length painted at least once. Overlapping intervals must be counted only once.

title: Weighted Schedule
statement: Each job is [start, end, reward] with start < end and nonnegative reward. Pick nonoverlapping jobs to maximize total reward. A job ending when another starts is compatible. Return 0 for no jobs.

title: Minimum Cover Window
statement: Return the shortest substring of s containing every character of t with its required multiplicity. If tied, return the earliest such substring. Return an empty string when no window exists or t is empty. Matching is case-sensitive.
